title: private/installer: expose lightweight installer health metrics endpoint for dashboards + validation
author: Bruno Silva
body:
Problem: Private installs currently lack a stable, scrapeable signal for installer/upgrade controller health. This blocks the “Private install health” dashboard work in observability-pack and makes the validation harness brittle (it has to infer progress from logs). We also saw a related failure mode in SUP-2431 where alert rules didn’t load post-upgrade and we didn’t have a clean metric to confirm the installer stage + last successful apply.

This PR adds a small Prometheus metrics endpoint to the private installer controller component (the in-cluster controller deployed by the Private installer) so the min observability pack can ship a day-1 dashboard and the validation harness can do deterministic checks.

What’s included: (1) New HTTP listener (default :9108) serving /metrics (promhttp) and /healthz (basic liveness) (2) A minimal, low-cardinality metric set under the redwood_installer_* namespace (3) Guardrails: no secrets, no per-resource labels, and bounded component labels (4) Documentation for enabling/disabling and scrape configuration.

Metrics emitted (v1): - redwood_installer_info{version,git_sha,bundle_version} 1 - redwood_installer_apply_in_progress (gauge 0/1) - redwood_installer_last_apply_success_timestamp_seconds (gauge) - redwood_installer_last_apply_duration_seconds (gauge) - redwood_installer_last_apply_result{result="success|error"} (gauge 0/1; only one series is 1) - redwood_installer_stage{stage="download|render|apply|verify|complete"} (gauge; only one stage is 1) - redwood_installer_component_ready{component="gateway|runtime|control_plane|grafana|prometheus|log_collector"} (gauge 0/1) - redwood_installer_rule_load_errors_total (counter)

Config: - INSTALLER_HEALTH_METRICS_ENABLED (default true for private builds; no-op for hosted) - INSTALLER_HEALTH_METRICS_ADDR (default 0.0.0.0:9108) - INSTALLER_HEALTH_METRICS_PATH (default /metrics)

Security notes: This is intended for in-cluster scraping only. The endpoint exposes coarse health/state + versions only; no customer identifiers, tokens, URLs, or per-tenant data. Network policy / ServiceMonitor selection should restrict access to the monitoring namespace (handled in installer/chart work).

Testing: - Unit tests verify stage mapping, component readiness gauge bounds, and that we never emit unbounded label values. - Integration test spins up the controller, simulates apply lifecycle transitions, scrapes /metrics, and asserts required series exist.

Follow-ups (out of scope here): - Dashboard panels + alerts (observability-pack PR-325/323) - Installer post-install validation command uses these metrics (redwood-private-installer PR-908) - Consider adding histogram buckets for apply duration once we have more field data (noise/cardinality review first).

Release notes: Private only. Adds installer health metrics endpoint for the Private observability minimum pack dashboard and validation harness.
commits: private/installer-controller: add healthmetrics registry and lifecycle hooks
private/installer-controller: serve promhttp /metrics and /healthz on dedicated listener
tests: add metrics endpoint integration test + label cardinality guardrail tests
docs: add installer health metrics config notes
illustrative_snippet:
New endpoint wiring (simplified):

// private/installer-controller/internal/server/server.go
mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.Handle(metricsPath, promhttp.HandlerFor(registry, promhttp.HandlerOpts{}))
mux.HandleFunc("/healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) { w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK) })

srv := &http.Server{Addr: metricsAddr, Handler: mux, ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second}
go func() { _ = srv.ListenAndServe() }()

Metric naming + bounded labels:

redwood_installer_component_ready{component="gateway"} 1
redwood_installer_stage{stage="apply"} 1
redwood_installer_last_apply_success_timestamp_seconds 1739311027
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we confirm labels are bounded? I don’t want env/cluster/tenant labels sneaking in. Also please align namespace with the minimum signals standard (redwood_installer_* is fine; avoid generic “health_*”).

Bruno Silva (author): Yep — component and stage are enums, result is an enum. No cluster/tenant labels. Added a unit test that fails if any label value is not in the allowed set. Also renamed two metrics from installer_health_* to redwood_installer_*.

Sean Gallagher (review): For dashboards we’ll want “last successful apply” and “apply in progress.” Please ensure last_apply_success_timestamp only updates on success (not every attempt). Also add a counter for rule load errors; that’s been a recurring cause of silent failures.
Bruno Silva (author): Updated: last_apply_success_timestamp_seconds is only set on success. Added redwood_installer_rule_load_errors_total and wired it to the rule loader error path.

Ethan Park (review): Any risk this leaks bundle versions that customers consider sensitive? (Probably fine, but want it explicitly stated.) Also, bind address default should be 0.0.0.0 only if a ServiceMonitor is created; otherwise prefer localhost.

Bruno Silva (author): Added explicit note in docs: bundle_version is the Redwood pack version only (no customer identifiers). On bind addr: changed default to 0.0.0.0 for private controller deployments (since it’s scraped via ClusterIP + NetworkPolicy); in non-private builds the server doesn’t start. Added INSTALLER_HEALTH_METRICS_ADDR override to set 127.0.0.1 if needed.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI looks good. Can we add an integration test that actually scrapes the endpoint and asserts the required series exist? This will help ENG-2847 harness assumptions.

Bruno Silva (author): Added integration/metrics_endpoint_test.go that runs the controller server, simulates lifecycle transitions, scrapes /metrics, and asserts presence of: installer_info, stage, apply_in_progress, and component_ready.
Allison Grant (review): Approved with the rename + bounded-label test, thanks.
Sean Gallagher (review): Approved. Please ping once observability-pack panels land so we can verify naming/queries.
Bruno Silva (author): Will do; coordinating with Sergio on the dashboard queries.
